corrections.issue: Mixes Kaastrup-Larsen's tongue-in-cheek speculation with his history and drops the Bridgewater caveat: he said managers 'could be a little bit facetious' that lower leverage let them manage more money, and the 400bn includes about 150bn of Bridgewater not in the 1990 figure.
corrections.fix: CTA volatility of 20-25% was normal in 1990 when the industry was under $10bn; institutionalisation from 2000 pushed managers to lower volatility, possibly (his speculation) also because lower leverage allows more capital to be managed; the quoted $400bn includes about $150bn of Bridgewater.

corrections.issue: The speaker said his own UCITS product runs at the lower end of volatility; 15-16% is where later entrants sit just below the VaR limit, i.e. roughly the cap.
corrections.fix: UCITS VaR limits prevent full leverage: UCITS CTA products are capped at roughly 15-16% annualised volatility (the Kaastrup-Larsen firm's own UCITS product is at the lower end), versus 20%+ in unregulated versions.

completeness_estimate: 0.65 - first reader got the main macro, carry, trend-update and Asness arguments; it missed several supporting data points, positioning/flow mechanisms, and some views and caveats.
